contributions.statement: Do not accept an agent-written function comment because a same-model judge says it matches the body: regenerate the body from the comment plus the rest of the file and require the existing tests to pass, since that judge was right for only 66.4% of the comments it accepted, and the generate-judge-revise loop still reached test agreement on only 127/238 functions (53.4%) versus 81/238 (34.0%) for a one-shot comment.
contributions.evidence: Table 2 and §4.2. Ground truth is test agreement on functions with at least 50% coverage (median 9 lines, §4.1.1), so weak tests can mark a wrong body as equivalent. One model (gpt-4.1-nano), one run, Python only. Failures still emit a best-effort comment, which is included in the 53.4%.
relative_to: Allamanis et al. 2024 round-trip correctness, cited in §5.2
an unvalidated same-model judge is not an accept gate

contributions.statement: Do not ship equivalence-style comments as a comprehension aid on helpfulness ratings alone: 11 developers who could still read the source showed identical total time (6.48 vs 6.48 min) and slightly worse understanding time (2.18 vs 1.94 min), while edit correctness was never reported.
contributions.evidence: Table 5 and §4.7. Understanding-helpfulness rose from 2.58 to 3.76 (p=0.0004); modifying-helpfulness 2.15 to 2.85 (p=0.0425) does not survive a 7-test correction. Within-subject data were tested with Mann-Whitney U. Participants were not blinded, and the treatment comment is visibly longer.
relative_to: 2607.26375 perceived help and measured comprehension diverge

contributions.statement: Do not expect a comment written so the model can rebuild the body to be shorter than the code: the length cap that worked best is 1× the function, the median function is 9 lines, and on tests the model already solves when shown the code the comment reaches 74.2% of assertions against an implicit 100% for the source.
contributions.evidence: §2.2.4 and Fig. 15 (1× best; the figure's rates are not printed). §4.1.1 median 9 lines, range 2–168. Table 3: 356/480 assertions (74.2%) after dropping tests the model cannot solve with the implementation visible.
relative_to: a paraphrase as long as the code does not save a reader from reading the code

reason: The test-checked round trip, with a same-model judge that is wrong about one time in three, is a gate a team can apply to agent-written function comments. The human-study and length results only bound that gate: perceived help did not change task time, and the comment is not a shorter substitute for the code.
